title: Organizing Unstructured Image Collections using Natural Language

bias_targets.methodology: Automatic discovery of bias dimensions using an open-ended semantic clustering framework on text-to-image outputs, quantifying bias intensity via the normalized entropy of cluster distributions, and measuring spurious correlations (e.g., with hair color) using normalized mutual information.

Clustering text-to-image model outputs for specific occupations and calculating the normalized entropy of the racial distribution to quantify bias intensity, followed by validation through a human evaluation study.
Applying open-ended semantic clustering to generated occupation portraits to identify age-based groups, and determining bias intensity and direction using normalized entropy.
Automatically extracting skin tone distributions from text-to-image generated occupation images via semantic clustering and calculating bias intensity scores using normalized entropy.

Discovering novel physical biases by grouping unstructured image collections into semantic clusters (e.g., beard/mustache, hair color) and identifying highly skewed cluster distributions as the bias direction.
Utilizing an exploratory clustering framework to uncover previously unstudied contextual and behavioral biases in text-to-image generations, evaluating bias severity through distribution entropy.
